Lussekatter (St. Lucia Buns)

Served at: Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil) · St. Lucia's Day

Makes about 24 bunsPrep 45 min active, plus 2-3 hours risingCook 10-15 min

Lussekatter, or St. Lucia Buns, are traditional saffron-infused sweet buns enjoyed during Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil) and St. Lucia's Day on December 13th in Sweden and other Nordic countries. Their distinctive S-shape and golden hue, from the saffron, symbolize light during the darkest time of the year, bringing warmth and cheer to the holiday season.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk
  • 1/2 teaspoon (0.5 g) saffron threads, crushed
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon (3 g) salt
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • 1 large egg, at room temperature
  • 4 1/2 to 5 cups (540-600 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) raisins, for decoration
  • 1 large egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon water or milk (for egg wash)

Method

  1. Gently warm the milk in a small saucepan until it is lukewarm (105-115°F / 40-46°C). Add the crushed saffron threads to the warm milk and let steep for 10 minutes.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the warm saffron milk, yeast, 1/4 cup (50 g) of the sugar, and salt. Let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
  3. Stir in the melted butter and the 1 large egg (at room temperature) into the yeast mixture.
  4. Gradually add the flour, about 1 cup (120 g) at a time, mixing until a soft dough forms. You may not need all 5 cups of flour; the dough should be slightly sticky but manageable.
  5. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, until smooth and elastic. If using a stand mixer, knead with the dough hook for 6-8 minutes.
  6. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  7. Punch down the dough and divide it into 24 equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each piece into a 8-10 inch (20-25 cm) rope.
  8. Shape each rope into an 'S' by coiling both ends inward towards the center. Place two raisins in the center of each coil, one in each 'eye' of the 'S'.
  9. Arrange the shaped buns on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and let rise for another 30-45 minutes, or until puffy.
  10. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
  11. Brush the risen buns with the egg wash.
  12. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown. Let cool on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • For a more intense saffron flavor and color, steep the saffron in a tablespoon of spirits (like vodka or brandy) for 30 minutes before adding it to the warm milk.
  • Do not overheat the milk for the yeast; if it's too hot, it will kill the yeast. It should feel warm, not hot, to the touch.
  • Lussekatter are best enjoyed fresh, but can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or frozen for longer storage.
